q: Compare actual and expected average attendance for the five AL East teams in 2025.

chart.title: Actual and expected attendance by team name

title: AL East actual and expected attendance, 2025
report: Only the Boston Red Sox beat their expected home attendance in the AL East in 2025, averaging 34,278 fans per game, which was 511 fans or 1.5% above expectations and represented 90.8% of capacity[1]. The New York Yankees led the division in raw turnout with 42,408 fans per game, but this fell 827 fans or 1.9% short of their expected 43,235 average, reaching 91.1% of capacity[1]. The Toronto Blue Jays averaged 35,184 fans, trailing their expected 36,823 average by 1,639 fans or 4.5% at 89.9% of capacity[1]. The Baltimore Orioles averaged 22,546 fans, which was 3,174 fans or 12.3% below their expected 25,720 average and represented 49.9% of capacity[1]. For the Tampa Bay Rays, expected attendance is unknown because they played at Steinbrenner Field, a temporary park, but they averaged 9,713 fans at 88.1% of capacity[1].

q: Do popular teams explain the link between crowds and TV audiences?
title: Popular teams attendance and TV audiences, 2024 to 2026
report:
Yes, games with smaller crowds tended to have smaller national TV audiences, but a crowd that was small for its own park did not clearly mean a smaller audience[1]. Comparing games on the same network, the two moved together (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62)[1]. After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, the link mostly disappears (0.16 in 2025, range -0.05 to 0.37; 0.14 in 2026, range -0.08 to 0.34; both ranges include zero)[1]. Across team-seasons, teams with bigger average crowds also had bigger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.52, n = 56, range 0.30 to 0.69), which is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size driving both, though the data does not prove the cause[2].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like.*

title: What drives MLB attendance, 2024 to 2026

q: How did Yankees national TV audiences change from 2025 to 2026?
title: Yankees national TV audience, 2025 vs 2026
report:
The New York Yankees saw their average national TV audience grow by 533,238 viewers from 2025 to 2026, reaching an average of 1,694,167 viewers per single game in 2026 compared to 1,160,929 viewers in 2025, though Nielsen changed its method in September 2025, which generally raised sports audiences[1]. The team's national TV presence expanded from 19 appearances in 2025 to 22 appearances in 2026[1]. This footprint included 14 single games and 5 Fox window games in 2025, compared to 17 single games and 5 Fox window games in 2026[1]. The Yankees' peak audience also climbed, with their highest single-game viewership rising from 2,784,000 viewers in 2025 to 3,616,000 viewers in 2026[1]. This growth coincided with a broader broadcast footprint; their network mix shifted from TBS (7 games), ESPN (5), Fox (5), and FS1 (2) in 2025 to TBS (8), Fox (5), NBC (3), ESPN (2), FS1 (2), ABC (1), and Netflix (1) in 2026[1].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons.*

q: Compare the Cubs and White Sox on attendance and national TV audiences in 2025.
title: Cubs and White Sox attendance and TV, 2025
report:
The Chicago Cubs dominated Chicago's sports landscape in 2025, outdrawing the Chicago White Sox by an average of 19,187 fans per game and capturing 17 national TV appearances while the White Sox had none in the data[1][2]. The Cubs averaged 37,259 fans per game (expected: 36,939) at 89.9% of capacity, whereas the White Sox averaged 18,072 fans (expected: 19,620) at 45.0% of capacity[3]. On television, the Cubs averaged 1,030,818 viewers across 12 single-game national broadcasts, peaking with 2,041,000 viewers on ESPN for an April 13 game against the Los Angeles Dodgers[2][4]. Their July 1 broadcast on TBS drew 374,000 viewers, which is main-network only because the truTV simulcast number is missing[4]. The Cubs also appeared in five regional Fox windows, which have no individual game viewership in the data; for instance, their May 10 window reached 80% of the country and drew 2,059,000 total viewers alongside the San Francisco Giants at Minnesota Twins game[4]. The White Sox had no national TV appearances in the data for 2025[2].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons.*
